title: ICM Messenger
description: A messenger deployed on two Avalanche chains that trust each other over Interchain Messaging (Teleporter). Messages carry their author, the receiver authenticates the counterpart, and relayer fees are optional.
prompts: Send a message from the C-Chain to my L1
Build cross-chain messaging between two Avalanche chains
How do I make my L1 contract react to something on the C-Chain?

source.description: Chain the first message is sent from

destination.description: Chain that receives it; must differ from source

params.name: owner
params.description: Owns both messengers and manages trusted remotes

params.name: message
params.description: Text of the smoke-test message, at most 280 bytes

prerequisites: Both chains have the TeleporterMessenger: true on Fuji C-Chain, Echo and Dispatch, and on an L1 launched with interoperability enabled
A relayer serving both chains: l1-quickstart with enableManagedRelayer sets one up, otherwise use the console's managed relayer
Native gas on both chains for the signer

contracts.name: ICMMessenger
contracts.description: Sends and receives authenticated text messages over Teleporter

contracts.name: TeleporterMessenger
contracts.description: Used to decode sent messages and to confirm delivery with messageReceived

steps.title: Make sure a relayer serves both chains
Deploy the messenger on the source chain
Deploy the messenger on the destination chain
Transfer the source messenger to its owner
Transfer the destination messenger to its owner
Wait for the relayer to deliver it

review: receiveTeleporterMessage rejects callers other than the TeleporterMessenger and origins that are not trusted remotes.
Both sides trust exactly one counterpart, identified by blockchain ID in hex and contract address.
DEFAULT_GAS_LIMIT (300,000) is about twice the measured cost of a first delivery of a 280-byte message; raise it if the receiver does more work.
Blockchain IDs are passed as 32-byte hex, not the CB58 strings the console shows.

frontend.summary: Chat between two chains: write on one, see it arrive on the other.
audience: People sending messages or commands between the C-Chain and an L1
journeys: Two columns, one per chain, each with its received messages and a message box.
Send and watch the message go from Sent to Delivered, usually within seconds while a relayer runs, with a link to the ICM explorer.
When delivery is slow, explain that a relayer carries messages and link its status, instead of showing an error.
flows: Send with sendMessage(destinationBlockchainID, destination, text, 0x0, 0, 0) on the source chain; read messageId from MessageSent.
Show delivery status by polling messageReceived(messageId) on the destination TeleporterMessenger, and link the message page on the Builder Hub explorer.
Render the destination feed from MessageReceived events; lastMessage() gives the newest one without an indexer.
Let the owner manage trusted remotes from an admin tab; never auto-trust addresses typed by users.
